QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_41

question.text: Maximum Drawdown (MDD) of an AIF is calculated as:

answer.text: Standard deviation of negative returns only
The difference between Gross IRR and Net IRR

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Ch 9.6.3: MDD = (Trough Value − Peak Value) / Peak Value, expressed as % of peak. Measures peak-to-trough decline, regardless of frequency or recovery time. **The Trap:** Option A is downside deviation (Sortino input). Option C is fee drag. Option D is single-day, not peak-to-trough. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B covers MDD; XXI-B similar; VIII (Derivatives) adapts for derivative portfolios. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** MDD does NOT tell you recovery time. Pair with 'time-to-recover' metric — some LPs weigh recovery time more than depth. Quote MDD against the benchmark MDD (Example 9.9 compared Fund PQR -13.71% with NIFTY -38.78%).
